t0: Who may change toggles and how, the keys applications read them with, and the changes scheduled for later.
t1: On by default, and the team in charge. A reason is asked for every change; an approval by someone else in a protected {environment}. Turning one down needs a reason and is recorded; a level above can lock one.
t3: Changing safeguards needs the admin role on
t4: A server key is a secret: it reads every rule, for one {environment}. A client key is public and can only ask for values of the toggles you made visible. Neither can change anything.
t5: Listing keys needs the operator role.
t6: Make a server key for a service that reads toggles, or a client key for a web page.
t7: Nothing is scheduled. Set a time when changing a toggle to make it then.
t9: Websites allowed to use it (addresses, separated by spaces)
t10: A reason is required for every change
t11: A change waits for another person's approval
t12: Mark the {environment} as watched for this many minutes after a change
t13: Lock these settings for everything below this level
t14: (required: you are turning a safeguard down)
